solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bad carrying on with a criminal

indicators.note: one word carrying another holds it within, so ILL is split to take the rest

parts.note: bad means ill, as in ill feeling
the on side in cricket is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Someone notorious for bad behaviour keeps company with a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' looks like part of the story but is the containment signal; 'on' is the cricket term, easy to read as a mere link.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal as an adjective describes acts against the law, a straight synonym of unlawful.

clue.text: Performing very well at home, showing class after penalty

indicators.note: class comes after penalty in the answer, so the pieces join in that order

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
a fine is a monetary penalty
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A team plays splendidly on home ground, showing quality after a spot kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in fine form is an idiom for being at one's best.

clue.text: Band on river vessel

parts.note: a line is a band or stripe

explanation.surface: Musicians are playing aboard a riverboat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places LINE on top of R.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Adorn country mansion where the "King" lived

parts.note: to grace is to adorn or decorate
a land is a country

explanation.surface: Decorating a rural estate once owned by royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley, whose Memphis home was Graceland.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceland is the Memphis mansion of Elvis Presley, nicknamed the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Find the Parisian sheltering old domestic pet

indicators.note: to shelter something is to keep it inside, so the French word encloses the rest

parts.note: le is French for the
a cat is a common household pet

explanation.surface: Track down the Frenchman who is giving refuge to an ageing house cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheltering' puts O + CAT between L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate is to discover where something is.

clue.text: A route abroad

parts.note: a route is a way to somewhere

explanation.surface: A traveller picks a path that leads overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abroad is out of their own country, which is to say they are travelling or living elsewhere.

clue.text: Wally in the role of head of state

parts.note: as means acting in the role of, as in playing as captain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A fool acting as president of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a silly, foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a fool, and wally is British slang for exactly that sort of fool.

clue.text: Call to account US soldier over in Scottish isle

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned over, so the soldier's letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: An American serviceman is held to account on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses only the soldier, which suits a down clue; 'in' then places him on the island, which lies in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to bring someone before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Article by female supporter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written by a woman who backs a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just sets the two pieces side by side; the answer puts F first.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiast who follows and backs a team or performer.

clue.text: Strange crest dividing a New York family

indicators.note: a piece dividing another sits between its letters, here splitting A and NY
strange signals the letters of the word crest are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd coat of arms splits a New York clan's history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' gives the jumble CESTR; 'dividing' wedges it between the first letter and the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is one's line of descent, the forebears of a family taken together.

clue.text: Also short of rum, et cetera

parts.note: and means also, in addition

indicators.note: rum is old slang for odd or strange, so the letters before it are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Low on rum, plus everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the anagram signal: SHORTOF becomes SOFORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: And so forth is the English equivalent of the Latin et cetera, meaning and the rest.

clue.text: Look after harbour

definitions.meaning: to tend or care for someone
to ... a grudge is to harbour it, keeping it alive

explanation.surface: A port official keeps an eye on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verb senses: caring for a patient and nursing a feeling one keeps inside.

clue.text: Training in it out at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors learn their trade while aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges INITOUT; 'out' belongs to the anagram fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, the training a student receives.

clue.text: Popular extract, basically

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
an essence is a concentrated extract

explanation.surface: A well-liked concentrate, put simply.
explanation.definitionFit: In essence means fundamentally, at its core.

clue.text: Number picked up by remote Scottish town

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the number is taken by its sound only

parts.note: four is a number
remote means far away

explanation.surface: A digit caught by some distant Scottish place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' gives FOR, sounding like four. Forfar is a town in Angus, eastern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Forfar is a market town in Angus, home of the Forfar bridie pastry.

clue.text: Originally, over in New Street finds badge

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are set out in a fresh arrangement
originally points to the start of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: Somewhere new, a sought-after emblem turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' takes O from 'over'; with STREET it makes OSTREET, which 'New' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge, given as a prize or worn to show support.

clue.text: Group round bar suffering reversal in game

indicators.note: the whole combination undergoes a reversal, being written from end to start
the group goes round the bar, enclosing it

parts.note: a set is a group of things
an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A band gathered round a pub counter has a setback in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' builds SINNET first; 'suffering reversal' then applies to that whole word, not just the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a game played across a net.

clue.text: Extremely furtive row of cats

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a line is a row

explanation.surface: A sneaky queue of moggies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes FE, the outer letters of 'furtive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline is the adjective relating to the cat family.

clue.text: Remainder live around university

indicators.note: the word for live wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: The rest of one's life is spent near a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts U inside RESIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over after the main part has gone, the remainder.

clue.text: Man, crook

definitions.meaning: to man, as in manning a desk

explanation.surface: A villain, described in two terse words.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb of providing workers; the other is the hooked stick a shepherd carries.

clue.text: Greek character in hotel in mountain area

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: an Alp is a high mountain
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is staying at a mountain lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts H between ALP and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Horse: lad astride big one

indicators.note: a rider astride something has it between their legs, so the lad's letters flank the rest

parts.note: a son is a lad
tall means big in height
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy sits on a huge mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' is apt: the lad's letters straddle the rest as a rider straddles a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, kept for breeding.

clue.text: Rent part of vaudeville theatre

indicators.note: part of signals the answer lies inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Leasing a section of an old music hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' finds LET across vaudevilLE Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property is to rent it out to a tenant.

clue.text: Standard cut reduced

indicators.note: reduced means shortened, losing its last letter here

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: The usual cutback has been made smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the final E of PARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or expected level, as in up to par or below par.

clue.text: Joke made by judge is French

parts.note: est is French for is

explanation.surface: A magistrate cracks a quip in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a quip or prank, something said in fun.

clue.text: Rot in heart of beech and another couple of trees

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre letter, here the third of five

parts.note: yew and ash are two more trees beside the beech

explanation.surface: Decay at the core of one tree spreads to two others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes E, the middle letter of BEECH; YEW and ASH follow. 'Rot' here means nonsense, not decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or humbug, talk meant to deceive, just as rot is.
